runs.u: Name a type of cloud.
runs.reply:
Cumulus — those puffy, cotton-ball clouds you often see on fair-weather days. They form from rising warm air and can grow into towering cumulonimbus clouds that bring thunderstorms.

Other common types include cirrus (thin and wispy, high altitude), stratus (flat gray layers that often bring drizzle), and nimbostratus (thick, rain-producing layers).

runs.u: Name a type of cloud.
runs.reply:
Cumulus — these are the puffy, cotton-like clouds you often see on fair-weather days, with flat bases and billowing tops.

Some other common types include cirrus (thin and wispy, high in the sky), stratus (flat, gray layers that can cover the whole sky), and cumulonimbus (towering thunderstorm clouds).
